sentences.zh: 親征凱旋命將出征奏凱受降獻俘受俘大閱會閱暨京師訓練附主

translations.literal: Personally leading campaigns; triumphant return; commissioning generals for expedition; reporting victory; receiving surrender; presenting captives; receiving captives; grand review; joint review; and capital training—with main sections appended.
translations.idiomatic: Personally Leading Campaigns; Triumphant Return; Commissioning Generals for Expedition; Reporting Victory; Receiving Surrender; Presenting Captives; Receiving Captives; Grand Review; Joint Review; and Capital Training—with the main sections appended

sentences.zh: 秋獮日食救護

translations.literal: Autumn hunt; solar eclipse rescue rites.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn Hunt; Solar Eclipse Rescue Rites

sentences.zh: 三曰軍禮。

translations.literal: The third is military rites.
translations.idiomatic: The third category is military rites.

sentences.zh: 國之大事，在祀與戎。

translations.literal: The great affairs of the state lie in sacrifice and war.
translations.idiomatic: The great affairs of a state lie in sacrifice and war.

sentences.zh: 周官制六軍，司九伐，權屬司馬。

translations.literal: The Offices of Zhou established six armies and supervised the nine punitive campaigns, with authority belonging to the Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou organized six armies and oversaw the nine punitive campaigns, with military authority vested in the Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 而大軍旅、大田役，其禮則宗伯掌之。

translations.literal: Yet the rites for great armies, great hunts, and corvée labor were administered by the Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the rites governing great armies, grand hunts, and corvée labor fell to the Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 是因治兵、振旅、茇舍、大閱之教，而寓蒐、苗、獮、狩之儀，以為社、礿、祊、烝之祭。

translations.literal: Thus the instruction in drilling troops, marshaling armies, encamping, and grand review embedded the ceremonies of spring hunt, summer hunt, autumn hunt, and winter hunt within the sacrifices of the community altar, seasonal sacrifices, branch sacrifices, and autumnal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Drilling troops, marshaling armies, encamping, and holding grand reviews were thereby taught, while the rituals of the spring, summer, autumn, and winter hunts were woven into the sacrifices at the community altar and the seasonal, branch, and autumnal rites.

sentences.zh: 如是，則講武為有名，而殺獸為有禮。

translations.literal: In this way military exercises had proper names, and the killing of game had proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In this way military exercises bore proper names, and the slaughter of game was invested with proper ritual.

sentences.zh: 有清武功燀赫，凡師征、受成、講肄、行圍諸禮節，厥制綦備。

translations.literal: Under the Qing, martial achievements blazed brilliantly; all ritual protocols for dispatching armies, receiving victory reports, military instruction, and hunting encampments were most fully established.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qing, martial glory shone brilliantly, and the ritual protocols for dispatching armies, receiving victory reports, military instruction, and hunting encampments were established in fullest detail.

sentences.zh: 爰溯古誼，分錄事要，著之於篇。

translations.literal: Here we trace ancient principles, record essential matters by category, and set them down in this treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Here we trace ancient principles, record the essential points by category, and set them down in this chapter.

sentences.zh: 古者日食救護，太僕贊鼓，亦屬夏官，今亦類附雲。

translations.literal: In antiquity solar-eclipse rescue rites, with the Grand Steward beating drums in accompaniment, also belonged to the Minister of War's office; they are likewise appended here by category.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, solar-eclipse rescue rites—with the Grand Steward beating drums in accompaniment—also fell under the Minister of War; they are likewise appended here by category.

sentences.zh: 親征天命三年，太祖頒訓練兵法書，躬統步騎征明，謁堂子，書七恨告天，是親征所由始。

translations.literal: Personally leading campaigns: In the third year of Tianming, the Taizu issued a book of military training and tactics, personally commanded infantry and cavalry against Ming, visited the tangzi, wrote the Seven Grievances to announce to Heaven—this was the beginning of personally leading campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Personally Leading Campaigns: In the third year of Tianming, the Taizu promulgated a manual of military training and tactics, personally led infantry and cavalry against the Ming, visited the tangzi, and wrote the Seven Grievances to announce to Heaven—thus began the rite of the emperor's personal campaign.

sentences.zh: 崇德初元，太宗伐朝鮮，前期誓天、告廟，頒行軍律令，分兵為左右翼。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, the Taizong attacked Korea; beforehand he swore oaths to Heaven and announced at the ancestral temple, promulgated military regulations, and divided the army into left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde, the Taizong campaigned against Korea; beforehand he swore oaths to Heaven and announced the campaign at the ancestral temple, promulgated military regulations, and divided the army into left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 至日，駕出撫近門，陳鹵簿，吹螺奏樂。

translations.literal: On the appointed day the imperial carriage exited the Fujin Gate, displayed the imperial guard of honor, and conch shells were blown with music performed.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day the imperial procession exited the Fujin Gate, the guard of honor was arrayed, and conch shells sounded as music was played.

sentences.zh: 祗謁堂子，三跪九拜。

translations.literal: He reverently visited the tangzi and performed three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: He reverently visited the tangzi and performed three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 外建八纛，致祭如初。

translations.literal: Outside eight battle standards were erected, and sacrifices were offered as at the first ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Outside, eight battle standards were erected and sacrifices were offered as at the first ceremony.

sentences.zh: 禮畢啟行。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, the march began.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed, the army set out.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，討噶爾丹，躬率六師出中道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi, campaigning against Galdan, he personally led the six armies out by the central route.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi, campaigning against Galdan, the emperor personally led the six armies along the central route.

sentences.zh: 前三日，祭告郊、廟、太歲，屆期遣祭道路、砲、火諸神。

translations.literal: Three days before, sacrifices were announced at the suburban altar, ancestral temple, and Grand Year Star; when the day arrived, envoys were dispatched to sacrifice to the gods of roads, cannon, and fire.
translations.idiomatic: Three days beforehand, sacrifices were announced at the suburban altar, ancestral temple, and Grand Year Star; on the appointed day envoys were dispatched to sacrifice to the gods of roads, cannon, and fire.

sentences.zh: 帝御征衣佩刀，乘騎出宮，內大臣等翊衛。

translations.literal: The emperor wore campaign robes and girded a sword, mounted and rode out of the palace, with inner ministers and others flanking in guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor donned campaign robes and girded a sword, rode out of the palace on horseback, and was flanked by inner ministers and other guards.

sentences.zh: 午門鳴鐘鼓，軍士鳴角螺，祭堂子、纛神如儀。

translations.literal: At the Meridian Gate bells and drums sounded; soldiers sounded horns and conches; sacrifices to the tangzi and standard gods were performed according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At the Meridian Gate bells and drums sounded; soldiers sounded horns and conches; sacrifices to the tangzi and the standard gods were performed according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 導迎樂作，奏祐平章。

translations.literal: Guiding and welcoming music was performed, playing the Youping Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Guiding and welcoming music was performed, playing the Youping Zhang.

sentences.zh: 駕出都門，詣陳兵所，聲砲二。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage exited the capital gate, proceeded to the place where troops were arrayed, and two cannon were fired.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial procession exited the capital gate, proceeded to where the troops were arrayed, and two cannon were fired.

sentences.zh: 旗軍繼發，王公百官忌送。

translations.literal: Banner troops set out in succession; princes, dukes, and officials of all ranks saw him off.
translations.idiomatic: Banner troops set out in succession, and princes, dukes, and officials of every rank saw him off.

sentences.zh: 軍士整伍，以次扈蹕。

translations.literal: Soldiers aligned their ranks and in order escorted the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers aligned their ranks and escorted the imperial progress in proper order.

sentences.zh: 每舍周視地勢，御營建正中，各營環向，繚以幔城，南設旌門。

translations.literal: At each halt the terrain was surveyed all around; the imperial camp was built at the center, each camp facing inward in a ring, encircled by a curtain wall, with a banner gate set to the south.
translations.idiomatic: At each halt the terrain was surveyed on all sides; the imperial camp was pitched at the center, the other camps ringed around it enclosed by a curtain wall, with a banner gate set to the south.

sentences.zh: 遠斥堠，嚴刁斗。

translations.literal: Outposts were set far out, and watch-drums were strictly kept.
translations.idiomatic: Outposts were posted far out, and the watch-drums were kept with strict vigilance.

sentences.zh: 置巡警二十一所，內大臣等率親軍宿衛。

translations.literal: Twenty-one patrol stations were established; inner ministers and others led the imperial guard in night watch.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-one patrol stations were established, and inner ministers and others led the imperial guard in night watch.

sentences.zh: 外設網城，東、西、南三門。

translations.literal: Outside a net-wall camp was set up with gates to the east, west, and south.
translations.idiomatic: Outside, a net-wall camp was set up with gates to the east, west, and south.

sentences.zh: 巡警八所，護軍統領率羽林軍徼循。

translations.literal: Eight patrol stations were established; the commandant of the guard led the Forest Guard in patrol rounds.
translations.idiomatic: Eight patrol stations were established, and the commandant of the guard led the Forest Guard in patrol rounds.

sentences.zh: 禁語譁，稽出入。

translations.literal: Noisy talk was forbidden, and comings and goings were checked.
translations.idiomatic: Noisy talk was forbidden, and all comings and goings were inspected.

sentences.zh: 又外布幕為重營，設四門，重各置十人嚴守。

translations.literal: Further outside, curtains were spread to form an outer camp with four gates; at each gate ten men were posted for strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: Further outside, curtains were spread to form an outer camp with four gates, and ten men were posted at each gate for strict guard.

sentences.zh: 其從征各官，列幕重營外。

translations.literal: The various officials accompanying the campaign pitched their tents outside the outer camp.
translations.idiomatic: The various officials accompanying the campaign pitched their tents outside the outer camp.

sentences.zh: 大軍分翼牧馬，禁越次。

translations.literal: The great army pastured horses by wing, forbidding crossing out of order.
translations.idiomatic: The great army pastured horses by wing, with crossing out of assigned order forbidden.

sentences.zh: 駕駐行營，諸軍皆止。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage halted at the field camp, all armies stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession halted at the field camp, all armies stopped.

sentences.zh: 從官奏事如常。

translations.literal: Attending officials presented memorials as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Attending officials presented memorials as usual.

sentences.zh: 夜漏初下，嚴更鼓，斷行人，內外禁旅番巡。

translations.literal: When the first watch of the night fell, night-drums were sounded strictly, travelers were cut off, and inner and outer forbidden troops patrolled in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: When the first watch of the night fell, the night-drums were sounded strictly, travelers were barred, and inner and outer forbidden troops patrolled in rotation.

sentences.zh: 五漏交，御營鳴鐘，前營角聲起。

translations.literal: At the fifth watch the imperial camp sounded the bell and the vanguard camp raised horn calls.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth watch the imperial camp sounded the bell, and the vanguard camp raised horn calls.

sentences.zh: 初嚴，外營蓐食治裝；

translations.literal: At the first alert the outer camps took bed-meal and prepared equipment;
translations.idiomatic: At the first alert the outer camps took their bed-meal and prepared equipment;

sentences.zh: 再嚴，前軍拔營；

translations.literal: at the second alert the vanguard broke camp;
translations.idiomatic: at the second alert the vanguard broke camp;

sentences.zh: 三嚴，左右軍、後軍發輜重，從征官俟旌門外。

translations.literal: at the third alert the left and right armies and rear army sent out baggage trains, and campaign officials waited outside the banner gate.
translations.idiomatic: at the third alert the left and right armies and the rear army sent out the baggage trains, and campaign officials waited outside the banner gate.

sentences.zh: 辨色，舉砲警蹕。

translations.literal: At daybreak cannon were fired to warn of the imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak cannon were fired to warn that the imperial procession was moving.

sentences.zh: 六師所過，守土官迎本境，大吏則出境以迎，外籓王公暨所部紳耆跪接，悉同時巡儀。

translations.literal: Wherever the six armies passed, local officials welcomed them within their jurisdiction; great officials went beyond the border to welcome; foreign vassal princes and local gentry and elders knelt to receive them—all the same as for imperial tour rites.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the six armies passed, local officials welcomed them within their jurisdiction; senior officials went beyond the border to welcome them; foreign vassal princes together with local gentry and elders knelt to receive the emperor—all following the same protocol as for an imperial tour.

sentences.zh: 軍行，隨時遣祭風、雨、山、川諸神，軍中堠望。

translations.literal: As the army marched, sacrifices were dispatched at appropriate times to the gods of wind, rain, mountains, and rivers, and beacon towers were manned in the army.
translations.idiomatic: As the army marched, sacrifices were dispatched at appropriate times to the gods of wind, rain, mountains, and rivers, and beacon towers were manned throughout the army.

sentences.zh: 聖祖躬巡，整軍伍，御旌門，簡閱將士，至西巴台，使者奉敕諭噶爾丹。

translations.literal: The Sage Ancestor personally toured, arrayed the army ranks, attended at the banner gate, inspected generals and soldiers; reaching Xibatai, an envoy bore an imperial edict to instruct Galdan.
translations.idiomatic: The Sage Ancestor personally toured the army, arrayed the ranks, attended at the banner gate, and inspected generals and soldiers; reaching Xibatai, an envoy bore an imperial edict addressed to Galdan.

sentences.zh: 敵望見大軍，棄甲走，帝率前軍長驅拖諾，分遣將軍進躡，乃還。

translations.literal: The enemy, seeing the great army, cast off armor and fled; the emperor led the vanguard in a long drive to Tuonuo, dispatched generals in pursuit, and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, seeing the great army, cast off their armor and fled; the emperor led the vanguard in a long drive to Tuonuo, dispatched generals in pursuit, and then returned.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹未悛，是歲秋，駕巡北邊，聲出塞試鷹，減從。

translations.literal: Galdan had not yet repented; that autumn the imperial carriage toured the northern frontier, publicly announcing a departure beyond the passes to try falconry, with a reduced retinue.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan had not yet submitted; that autumn the emperor toured the northern frontier, publicly announcing a departure beyond the passes to try falconry, with a reduced retinue.

sentences.zh: 十月，抵白塔，駐南關，蒙古王以下貢獻駱驛。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he reached Baita, encamped at Nanguan, and Mongol princes down to the commoners presented tribute in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he reached Baita, encamped at Nanguan, and Mongol princes down to the commoners presented tribute in unbroken succession.

sentences.zh: 帝賜戰勝兵士食，引近御坐遍賚之。

translations.literal: The emperor bestowed food on the victorious soldiers, drew them near the imperial seat, and rewarded them all in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bestowed food on the victorious soldiers, drew them near the imperial seat, and rewarded them all in turn.

sentences.zh: 次日，益徹御膳犒軍。

translations.literal: The next day he further sent out imperial meals to feast the army.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he further sent out imperial meals to feast the army.

sentences.zh: 逾月，至呼坦和碩，渡河，降者踵至。

translations.literal: After more than a month he reached Khutangheshuo, crossed the river, and submitters arrived one after another.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month he reached Khutangheshuo, crossed the river, and submitters arrived one after another.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹就撫，乃班師。

translations.literal: Galdan submitted to pacification, and the army was withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Galdan submitted to pacification, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝三駕北征，啟行如初禮，至橫城止。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor made his third northern campaign; departure followed the initial rites, and he halted at Hengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor made his third northern campaign; departure followed the initial rites, and he halted at Hengcheng.

sentences.zh: 令守土大臣臨河迎蹕。

translations.literal: He ordered local officials to welcome the imperial progress at the river.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered local officials to welcome the imperial progress at the river.

sentences.zh: 時哈密俘噶爾丹子送軍所，額魯特部多納款者，噶爾丹仰藥死，駕自黃河汎舟還。

translations.literal: At that time Hami delivered Galdan's son captive to the army; many of the Oirat tribes submitted; Galdan took poison and died; the imperial carriage returned by boat on the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Hami delivered Galdan's son as a captive to the army; many Oirat tribes submitted; Galdan took poison and died; and the emperor returned by boat on the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 凱旋崇德二年，太宗征服朝鮮。

translations.literal: Triumphant return: In the second year of Chongde the Taizong conquered Korea.
translations.idiomatic: Triumphant Return: In the second year of Chongde the Taizong conquered Korea.

sentences.zh: 班師日，其君臣出城十里外送駕，三跪九拜如禮。

translations.literal: On the day the army withdrew, their ruler and ministers went ten li beyond the city to send off the imperial carriage, performing three kneelings and nine prostrations according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the army withdrew, the Korean ruler and his ministers went ten li beyond the city to send off the emperor, performing three kneelings and nine prostrations according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 歸則遣大臣二人送之。

translations.literal: On returning, two great ministers were dispatched to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey, two great ministers were dispatched to escort them.

sentences.zh: 啟蹕，即軍前祭纛。

translations.literal: When the march resumed, sacrifices to the battle standards were immediately performed before the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the march resumed, sacrifices to the battle standards were immediately performed before the army.

sentences.zh: 守土官道迎，俟駕過，隨軍次承命，遙坐賜酒。

translations.literal: Local officials welcomed along the road; after the imperial carriage passed they followed the army's march to receive orders, sat at a distance, and were bestowed wine.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials welcomed them along the road; after the emperor passed they followed the army's march to receive orders, sat at a distance, and were bestowed wine.

sentences.zh: 將至盛京二十里，會鄭親王等齎奉賀表，遂先除道，張黃幄，俟駕至，伏迎道左。

translations.literal: When still twenty li from Shengjing, they met the Prince of Zheng and others bearing congratulatory memorials; they first cleared the road, spread a yellow canopy, and when the imperial carriage arrived prostrated themselves to welcome on the left of the road.
translations.idiomatic: When still twenty li from Shengjing, they met the Prince of Zheng and others bearing congratulatory memorials; the road was cleared first, a yellow canopy was spread, and when the emperor arrived they prostrated themselves to welcome him on the left of the road.

sentences.zh: 帝入幄坐，王等跪進表，大學士受之。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the canopy and sat; the princes knelt and presented the memorial; the grand secretary received it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the canopy and sat; the princes knelt and presented the memorial, which the grand secretary received.

sentences.zh: 宣讀畢，王等三跪九拜，乃大宴，宴罷啟行。

translations.literal: When the reading was finished the princes performed three kneelings and nine prostrations; then a great feast was held, and when the feast ended the march resumed.
translations.idiomatic: When the reading was finished the princes performed three kneelings and nine prostrations; then a great feast was held, and when the feast ended the march resumed.

sentences.zh: 至盛京，禮謁堂子，還宮。

translations.literal: On reaching Shengjing he performed rites at the tangzi and returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Shengjing he performed rites at the tangzi and returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十五年，聖祖征噶爾丹，破之，還蹕拖諾，捷入，焚香謝天。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi the Sage Ancestor campaigned against Galdan, defeated him, returned the imperial progress to Tuonuo; when victory news arrived he burned incense to thank Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year of Kangxi the Sage Ancestor campaigned against Galdan, defeated him, and returned the imperial progress to Tuonuo; when news of victory arrived he burned incense to thank Heaven.

sentences.zh: 入行營，大學士等進賀表，王公百官畢賀。

translations.literal: Entering the field camp, grand secretaries and others presented congratulatory memorials; princes, dukes, and officials of all ranks all offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the field camp, grand secretaries and others presented congratulatory memorials, and princes, dukes, and officials of every rank offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 留牧蒙古王等迎駕行禮，喀爾喀札薩克等集營東門請瞻覲，皆稽首呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Mongol princes who had remained to pasture welcomed the imperial carriage with ritual; Khalkha jasak and others gathered at the camp's east gate requesting audience, all kowtowing and shouting ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol princes who had remained to pasture welcomed the emperor with ritual; Khalkha jasak and others gathered at the camp's east gate to request an audience, all kowtowing and shouting "Ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 賜茶及宴，賚銀物有差。

translations.literal: Tea and banquets were bestowed; silver goods were granted in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Tea and banquets were bestowed, and silver goods were granted in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 沿途迎獻羅拜者，繦至輻湊。

translations.literal: Those who welcomed and presented tribute along the route, carrying children in swaddling-cloths, came in dense throngs like wheel hubs pressed together.
translations.idiomatic: Those who welcomed and presented tribute along the route, many carrying infants in swaddling-cloths, came in dense throngs.

sentences.zh: 至清河，皇子、王公暨群臣跪迎郊外五里，八旗軍校、近畿士民亦焚香懸采，扶攜俯伏。

translations.literal: At Qinghe, imperial sons, princes, and all ministers knelt to welcome five li beyond the suburbs; Eight Banner officers and soldiers and nearby commoners also burned incense and hung colored streamers, supporting one another as they prostrated themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinghe, imperial sons, princes, and all ministers knelt to welcome him five li beyond the suburbs; Eight Banner officers and soldiers and commoners of the nearby districts also burned incense and hung colored streamers, supporting one another as they prostrated themselves.

sentences.zh: 命前驅毋警蹕，環集至數百萬人，歡聲雷動。

translations.literal: He ordered the vanguard not to warn of the imperial progress; the crowd gathered to several million people, and cheers thundered like rolling drums.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the vanguard not to warn of the imperial approach; the crowd gathered to several million people, and cheers thundered like rolling drums.

sentences.zh: 帝謁堂子如儀。

translations.literal: The emperor visited the tangzi according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited the tangzi according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 明年，朔漠平，班師亦如之。

translations.literal: The next year the northern deserts were pacified, and the army withdrew with the same rites.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the northern deserts were pacified, and the army withdrew with the same rites.

sentences.zh: 還宮後，遣祭郊、社、宗廟，遍群神，謁陵寢，御殿受賀。

translations.literal: After returning to the palace, envoys were dispatched to sacrifice at the suburban altar, altars of soil and grain, and ancestral temple, to all the gods universally, to visit the imperial tombs, and to ascend the hall to receive congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: After returning to the palace, envoys were dispatched to sacrifice at the suburban altar, altars of soil and grain, and ancestral temple, to all the gods, to visit the imperial tombs, and to ascend the hall to receive congratulations.

sentences.zh: 直省官咸進表文，頒詔如制。

translations.literal: Officials of all provinces presented memorials; an edict was promulgated according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of all provinces presented memorials, and an edict was promulgated according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 帝自勒銘鑱石，並建碑太學雲。

translations.literal: The emperor himself carved inscriptions on stone, and also erected a stele at the Imperial Academy—thus.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself carved inscriptions on stone and also erected a stele at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 命將出征崇德初元，太宗命睿王多爾袞等出師征明，躬自臨送，祭堂子、纛神，如親征儀。

translations.literal: Commissioning generals for expedition: In the first year of Chongde the Taizong ordered the Prince Rui Dorgon and others to take the army out against Ming, personally came to send them off, and sacrificed at the tangzi and standard gods as in the personally-led campaign rites.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioning Generals for Expedition: In the first year of Chongde the Taizong ordered the Prince Rui Dorgon and others to march against the Ming, came in person to send them off, and sacrificed at the tangzi and the standard gods as in the rites for a personally led campaign.

sentences.zh: 遂至演武場，諭誡將士。

translations.literal: He then proceeded to the drill ground and admonished the generals and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He then proceeded to the drill ground and admonished the generals and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，命英王阿濟格為靖遠大將軍，征流寇，賜敕印。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi the Prince Ying Ajige was appointed Pacification-of-the-Distant Grand General to campaign against the roving bandits, and was granted the edict and seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shunzhi the Prince Ying Ajige was appointed Pacification-of-the-Distant Grand General to campaign against the roving bandits and was granted the edict and seal.

sentences.zh: 其儀，午門外具鹵簿，陛上張黃幄，設御座。

translations.literal: The ritual: outside the Meridian Gate the imperial guard of honor was arrayed; on the steps a yellow canopy was spread and the imperial seat set.
translations.idiomatic: For the ritual, outside the Meridian Gate the guard of honor was arrayed; on the steps a yellow canopy was spread and the imperial seat set.

sentences.zh: 陳敕印檐東案，王公百官會集。

translations.literal: The edict and seal were displayed on an eastern table under the eaves; princes, dukes, and officials of all ranks assembled.
translations.idiomatic: The edict and seal were displayed on a table under the eastern eaves, and princes, dukes, and officials of every rank assembled.

sentences.zh: 帝升座，大將軍率出征官詣拜位跪，內院大臣奉宣滿、蒙、漢三體敕書，授大將軍敕印，畢，啟行。

translations.literal: The emperor ascended the seat; the grand general led the expedition officers to the obeisance position and knelt; an inner-court minister proclaimed the edict in Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese, presented the edict and seal to the grand general, and when finished the march began.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ascended the seat; the grand general led the expedition officers to the obeisance position and knelt; an inner-court minister proclaimed the edict in Manchu, Mongol, and Chinese and presented the edict and seal to the grand general; when this was finished, the army set out.

sentences.zh: 十三年，定出師前一日，午門前例頒衣馬弓刀，並傳集出征各官，面授方略。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year it was fixed that one day before departure, at the Meridian Gate, clothing, horses, bows, and blades were customarily issued, and all expedition officers were summoned to receive strategy in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year it was fixed that one day before departure, at the Meridian Gate, clothing, horses, bows, and blades were customarily issued, and all expedition officers were summoned to receive strategy in person.

sentences.zh: 賜筵宴。

translations.literal: A banquet was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: A banquet was bestowed.

sentences.zh: 行日，咸戎服俟午門外，頒敕印如初禮。

translations.literal: On the day of departure all wore military dress and waited outside the Meridian Gate; the edict and seal were issued as in the initial ritual.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of departure all wore military dress and waited outside the Meridian Gate, and the edict and seal were issued as in the initial ritual.

sentences.zh: 康熙十三年，命將分出湖廣、四川。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi generals were commissioned and dispatched separately to Huguang and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Kangxi generals were commissioned and dispatched separately to Huguang and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，駕出長安右門送行。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed the imperial carriage exited the Chang'an Right Gate to send them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed the emperor exited the Chang'an Right Gate to send them off.

sentences.zh: 出征王率各官行至陳兵所，禮部設祖帳，光祿寺備茶酒，內大臣等奉引謝恩。

translations.literal: The expedition prince led the various officers to the place where troops were arrayed; the Ministry of Rites set up the farewell tent; the Court of Imperial Entertainments prepared tea and wine; inner ministers and others led them in offering thanks.
translations.idiomatic: The expedition prince led the various officers to where the troops were arrayed; the Ministry of Rites set up the farewell tent; the Court of Imperial Entertainments prepared tea and wine; and inner ministers and others led them in offering thanks.

sentences.zh: 首途，如故。

translations.literal: They set out on the road as before.
translations.idiomatic: They set out on the road as before.

sentences.zh: 或帝不親送，則令親王、內大臣往。

translations.literal: If the emperor did not personally send them off, then an imperial prince or inner minister was ordered to go.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor did not personally send them off, an imperial prince or inner minister was dispatched in his place.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹之役，先自歸化驛召費揚古為撫遠大將軍，至日賞宴，聖祖御太和門，大臣隅坐，其出征運糧大臣分坐金水橋北左右。

translations.literal: In the Galdan campaign, Fiyanggū was first summoned from the Guihua post station to be Pacification-of-the-Distant Grand General; on the appointed day a reward banquet was held; the Sage Ancestor attended at the Gate of Supreme Harmony, ministers sat to the sides, and the expedition grain-transport ministers sat separately to the left and right north of the Jinshui Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the Galdan campaign, Fiyanggū was first summoned from the Guihua post station to serve as Pacification-of-the-Distant Grand General; on the appointed day a reward banquet was held; the Sage Ancestor attended at the Gate of Supreme Harmony with ministers seated to the sides, and the expedition grain-transport ministers sat separately to the left and right north of the Jinshui Bridge.

sentences.zh: 作樂陳百戲，命大將軍進御前，親賜卮酒。

translations.literal: Music was performed and a hundred entertainments displayed; the grand general was ordered to advance before the emperor, who personally bestowed a cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: Music was performed and a hundred entertainments displayed; the grand general was ordered to advance before the emperor, who personally bestowed a cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 跪受叩飲訖，都統、副都統繼進，則令侍衛授酒。

translations.literal: He knelt to receive it, kowtowed, and finished drinking; when commandants and vice-commandants advanced in succession, attendants were ordered to present the wine.
translations.idiomatic: He knelt to receive it, kowtowed, and finished drinking; when commandants and vice-commandants advanced in succession, attendants were ordered to present the wine.

sentences.zh: 參領以下十人一列，跪飲階上而已。

translations.literal: Staff captains and below, ten men per row, knelt and drank on the steps only.
translations.idiomatic: Staff captains and below, ten men per row, knelt and drank on the steps only.

sentences.zh: 覆命大臣等遍視眾軍飲宴畢，賜與宴者御用蟒幣，餘賜幣，兵賜布。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the ministers and others to survey all the troops until the feast was finished; those who feasted were granted imperial python robes and silks; the rest were granted silks; soldiers were granted cloth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the ministers and others to see that all the troops had finished feasting; those who feasted were granted imperial python robes and silks, the rest were granted silks, and soldiers were granted cloth.

sentences.zh: 同謝恩出，大學士始以敕印授大將軍。

translations.literal: Together they offered thanks and departed; only then did the grand secretary present the edict and seal to the grand general.
translations.idiomatic: Together they offered thanks and departed; only then did the grand secretary present the edict and seal to the grand general.

sentences.zh: 雍正七年，定命將前一日告廟。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yongzheng it was fixed that one day before commissioning generals the ancestral temple was announced.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yongzheng it was fixed that one day before commissioning generals the ancestral temple was to be announced.

sentences.zh: 行日告奉先殿，並遣官。

translations.literal: On the day of departure the Hall of Ancestor Worship was announced, and an official was also dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of departure, announcement was made at the Hall of Ancestor Worship, and an official was dispatched as well.

sentences.zh: 若先出師疆埸，即軍前命為大將軍者，則命正、副使齎敕印往。

translations.literal: If troops had first been sent out to the border and one was appointed grand general before the army, then the chief and deputy envoys were ordered to carry the edict and seal there.
translations.idiomatic: If troops had already been dispatched to the frontier and a grand general was appointed at the front, the chief and deputy envoys were ordered to carry the edict and seal to him.

sentences.zh: 大將軍率屬俟教場，廳事設黃案，陳敕印。

translations.literal: The grand general led his subordinates to wait at the drill ground; in the reception hall a yellow desk was set up and the edict and seal displayed.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general led his subordinates to wait at the drill ground; in the reception hall a yellow desk was set up and the edict and seal were displayed.

sentences.zh: 大將軍跪，宣敕文正使授敕，宣印文副使授印，大將軍以次祗受，轉授左右從官，行三跪九叩禮。

translations.literal: The grand general knelt; the chief envoy read the edict text and conferred the edict, the deputy envoy read the seal text and conferred the seal; the grand general received them in turn, passed them to attendants left and right, and performed the three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: The grand general knelt; the chief envoy read the edict and conferred it, the deputy envoy read the seal text and conferred the seal; the grand general received them in turn, passed them to attendants on either side, and performed the three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 禮成，奉入大營。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, they were borne into the main camp.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed, the edict and seal were borne into the main camp.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十四年，定命將儀三：一曰授敕印，經略大將軍出師，皇帝臨軒頒給。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong, three rites for commissioning generals were fixed: first, bestowing the edict and seal—when the grand coordinator grand general set out, the emperor attended the front hall to issue them.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong, three rites for commissioning generals were established: first, bestowing the edict and seal—when the grand coordinator grand general set out on campaign, the emperor attended the front hall to issue them.

sentences.zh: 二曰祓社，凡出師前期，告奉先殿，禮堂子，祭纛。

translations.literal: Second, purification at the altars of soil and grain—before every expedition, announce to the Hall of Ancestor Worship, perform rites at the tangzi, and sacrifice to the battle standards.
translations.idiomatic: Second, purification at the altars of soil and grain—before every expedition, announcement was made at the Hall of Ancestor Worship, rites were performed at the tangzi, and sacrifices were offered to the battle standards.

sentences.zh: 三曰祖道，經略啟行，皇帝親餞賜酒，命大臣送郊外，具祖帳暨宴，儀並詳前。

translations.literal: Third, the farewell rite—when the grand coordinator set out, the emperor personally offered a parting toast and wine, ordered ministers to escort him beyond the suburbs, provided the farewell tent and banquet—the rites are all detailed above.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the farewell rite—when the grand coordinator set out, the emperor personally offered a parting toast and bestowed wine, ordered ministers to escort him beyond the suburbs, and provided the farewell tent and banquet; the rites are all detailed above.

sentences.zh: 徂征儀二：一曰整旅，經略前隊列御賜軍械，次令箭，次敕印，次標旗，大隊軍旅殿。

translations.literal: Two rites for setting out on campaign: first, marshaling the troops—the grand coordinator's vanguard displayed imperially bestowed arms, then command arrows, then the edict and seal, then standard flags, with the main army bringing up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Two rites for setting out on campaign: first, marshaling the troops—the grand coordinator's vanguard displayed imperially bestowed arms, followed by command arrows, then the edict and seal, then standard flags, with the main army bringing up the rear.

sentences.zh: 令箭、標旗數皆十二。

translations.literal: The number of command arrows and standard flags was twelve each.
translations.idiomatic: The number of command arrows and standard flags was twelve each.

sentences.zh: 二曰守土官相見，經略過境，將軍、督、撫蟒服出郭迎候，文自司道、武自總兵以下，跽道右及廳事。

translations.literal: Second, meeting with territorial officials—when the grand coordinator passed through a jurisdiction, the general, governor-general, and governor, in python robes, went beyond the city wall to welcome him; civil officials from the surveillance commissioner and circuit intendant downward and military from the regional commander downward knelt on the right of the road and at the reception hall.
translations.idiomatic: Second, meeting with territorial officials—when the grand coordinator passed through a jurisdiction, the general, governor-general, and governor, in python robes, went beyond the city wall to welcome him; civil officials from the surveillance commissioner and circuit intendant downward and military officers from the regional commander downward knelt on the right of the road and at the reception hall.

sentences.zh: 經略正坐，將軍、督、撫側坐，文司道、武提督以下，行庭參禮。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator sat in the place of honor; the general, governor-general, and governor sat to the side; civil officials from the surveillance commissioner and circuit intendant and military from the provincial commander-in-chief downward performed the courtyard audience rite.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coordinator sat in the place of honor; the general, governor-general, and governor sat to the side; civil officials from the surveillance commissioner and circuit intendant downward and military officers from the provincial commander-in-chief downward performed the courtyard audience rite.

sentences.zh: 啟行候送如前儀。

translations.literal: When setting out, the escort and send-off followed the previous rites.
translations.idiomatic: When he set out, the escort and send-off followed the previous rites.

sentences.zh: 若頒敕印不御殿，即除鹵簿、樂懸，百官無職事者不會集。

translations.literal: If the edict and seal were issued without the emperor ascending the hall, then the imperial retinue and suspended music were omitted, and officials without duties did not assemble.
translations.idiomatic: If the edict and seal were issued without the emperor ascending the hall, the imperial retinue and suspended music were omitted, and officials without assigned duties did not assemble.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，命大學士傅恆經略雲南軍務，高宗不升殿，不禮堂子，不祭纛，不親送。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, Grand Secretary Fu Heng was ordered as grand coordinator for Yunnan military affairs; the Gaozong did not ascend the hall, did not perform rites at the tangzi, did not sacrifice to the standards, and did not personally send him off.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year, Grand Secretary Fu Heng was appointed grand coordinator for Yunnan military affairs; the Gaozong did not ascend the hall, did not perform rites at the tangzi, did not sacrifice to the battle standards, and did not personally send him off.

sentences.zh: 內閣學士奉敕印至太和殿，經略等先俟陛階，大學士二人立殿外。

translations.literal: A Hanlin Academician brought the edict and seal to the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the grand coordinator and others first waited at the steps; two grand secretaries stood outside the hall.
translations.idiomatic: A Hanlin Academician brought the edict and seal to the Hall of Supreme Harmony; the grand coordinator and others waited first at the steps, while two grand secretaries stood outside the hall.

sentences.zh: 屆時經略升陛，印官從大閣學士入奉敕印出，經略跪受。

translations.literal: When the time came the grand coordinator ascended the steps; the seal officer, following the grand Hanlin Academician, entered, bore out the edict and seal, and the grand coordinator knelt to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came the grand coordinator ascended the steps; the seal officer, following the grand Hanlin Academician, entered and bore out the edict and seal, and the grand coordinator knelt to receive them.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，奉敕印官前，經略後，及階下，置敕印采亭內，前張黃蓋，列御仗，從征侍衛前引，餘俱後隨，至經略第止。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, the bearer of the edict and seal went ahead and the grand coordinator followed; at the foot of the steps they were placed in the colored canopy sedan; a yellow parasol was displayed in front, imperial guards were arrayed, expedition attendants led in front, and the rest followed behind, continuing until the grand coordinator's residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed, the bearer of the edict and seal went ahead and the grand coordinator followed; at the foot of the steps the edict and seal were placed in the colored canopy sedan; a yellow parasol was displayed in front, imperial guards were arrayed, expedition attendants led the way, and the rest followed behind, continuing until the grand coordinator's residence.

sentences.zh: 敕印陳廳案上。

translations.literal: The edict and seal were displayed on the desk in the reception hall.
translations.idiomatic: The edict and seal were displayed on the desk in the reception hall.

sentences.zh: 屆日肅隊行。

translations.literal: On the appointed day he set out with his ranks in formal order.
translations.idiomatic: On the appointed day he set out with his ranks in formal order.

sentences.zh: 奏凱天聰初元，朝鮮奏捷，班師。

translations.literal: Reporting victory: In the first year of Tiancong, victory was reported from Korea, and the army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Reporting Victory: In the first year of Tiancong, victory was reported from Korea, and the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 車駕出城，頓武靖營野次。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage left the city and halted at a field camp at Wujing Camp.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage left the city and halted at a field encampment at Wujing Camp.

sentences.zh: 設行幄御營一里外，率諸貝勒逾行幄數武，立馬以待凱旋。

translations.literal: A traveling canopy was set up one li outside the imperial camp; leading the various beile, he went several wu beyond the traveling canopy, dismounted, and waited for the triumphant return.
translations.idiomatic: A traveling canopy was set up one li outside the imperial camp; leading the various beile, he went several wu beyond the traveling canopy, dismounted, and waited for the triumphant return.

sentences.zh: 既至，遂依次排列，立纛、拜天，入覲，帝出位迎之。

translations.literal: When they arrived, they were arrayed in order, erected the standards and bowed to Heaven, entered for audience, and the emperor left his place to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, they were arrayed in order, erected the standards and bowed to Heaven, entered for audience, and the emperor left his place to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 諸貝勒行跪拜禮，賜筵宴。

translations.literal: The various beile performed kneeling and prostration rites, and a banquet was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The various beile performed kneeling and prostration rites, and a banquet was bestowed.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年，征明凱旋，太宗率群臣出城十里迎勞，王、貝勒等依次成列，建纛鳴螺，帝率同拜天，三跪九叩。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongde, returning triumphant from the campaign against Ming, the Taizong led the civil and military officials ten li beyond the city to welcome and reward them; princes, beile, and others formed ranks in order, erected the standards and sounded conches; the emperor led them in bowing to Heaven with three kneelings and nine prostrations.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongde, returning triumphant from the campaign against the Ming, the Taizong led civil and military officials ten li beyond the city to welcome and reward them; princes, beile, and others formed ranks in order, erected the standards and sounded conches; the emperor led them in bowing to Heaven with three kneelings and nine prostrations.

sentences.zh: 畢，升座。

translations.literal: When finished, he ascended to his seat.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, he ascended to his seat.

sentences.zh: 王、貝勒進獻捷表，大學士接受，奉御前讀訖，跪叩如儀。

translations.literal: Princes and beile advanced to present the victory memorial; the grand secretary received it, brought it before the emperor and read it through, then knelt and prostrated according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and beile advanced to present the victory memorial; the grand secretary received it, brought it before the emperor and read it through, then knelt and prostrated according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 頒旨行抱見禮。

translations.literal: An edict was issued ordering the embrace-audience rite.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued ordering the embrace-audience rite.

sentences.zh: 於是王、貝勒進御前一跪三叩，賜坐、設宴同。

translations.literal: Thereupon princes and beile advanced before the emperor, performed one kneeling and three prostrations, were granted seats, and a banquet was set as before.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon princes and beile advanced before the emperor, performed one kneeling and three prostrations, were granted seats, and a banquet was set as before.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，南京平，豫王班師還。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, Nanjing was pacified, and the Prince of Yu withdrew the army and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shunzhi, Nanjing was pacified, and the Prince of Yu withdrew the army and returned.

sentences.zh: 世祖赴南苑迎勞，樹十餘大纛，如初禮。

translations.literal: The Shizu went to the Southern Park to welcome and reward them, erected more than ten great standards, as in the original rites.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu went to the Southern Park to welcome and reward them, erected more than ten great standards, as in the original rites.

sentences.zh: 十三年，定制出征王大臣凱旋，遣王公一人偕大臣郊勞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year it was fixed by regulation that when expedition princes and grand ministers returned triumphant, one imperial prince together with a minister was dispatched to welcome them in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year it was established by regulation that when expedition princes and grand ministers returned triumphant, one imperial prince together with a minister was dispatched to welcome them in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，定凱旋次日，帝御殿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi it was fixed that on the day after the triumphant return the emperor attended the hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kangxi it was established that on the day after the triumphant return the emperor would attend the hall.

sentences.zh: 禮成。

translations.literal: The rites were completed.
translations.idiomatic: The rites were completed.

sentences.zh: 免將軍等行禮，筵宴免桌席，止宰牲。

translations.literal: The generals and others were exempted from performing rites; at the banquet table settings were omitted and only animals were slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: The generals and others were exempted from performing rites; at the banquet table settings were omitted and only animals were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，大將軍貝子章泰等自雲南奏凱，駕至盧溝橋迎勞駐蹕，有司治具，翼日駕蒞至，齊眾拜天，以為故事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Grand General Beile Zhangtai and others reported victory from Yunnan; the emperor went to the Lugou Bridge to welcome and reward them and made a halt; the responsible officials prepared the arrangements; the next day when the emperor arrived, all together bowed to Heaven, and this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, Grand General Beile Zhangtai and others reported victory from Yunnan; the emperor went to the Lugou Bridge to welcome and reward them and made a halt; the responsible officials prepared the arrangements; the next day when the emperor arrived, all together bowed to Heaven, and this became precedent.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十四年，定奏凱功成，祭告天地、廟社、陵寢，釋奠先師，勒碑太學，命儒臣輯平定方略垂奕。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong it was fixed that upon reporting victory after success, reports were made to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain, and the imperial tombs; libations were offered to the Sage Teacher; a stele was carved at the Imperial Academy; and Confucian officials were ordered to compile records of pacification to be passed down.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong it was established that upon reporting victory after success, reports were made to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple and altars of soil and grain, and the imperial tombs; libations were offered to the Sage Teacher; a stele was carved at the Imperial Academy; and Confucian officials were ordered to compile records of pacification to be transmitted to posterity.

sentences.zh: 經略大將軍師旋，將入城，遣廷臣郊勞，帝臨軒，經略率有功諸臣謝恩，繳印敕，儀同受敕。

translations.literal: When the grand coordinator grand general's army returned and was about to enter the city, court ministers were dispatched to welcome them in the suburbs; the emperor attended the front hall; the grand coordinator led meritorious officials in offering thanks; the seal and edict were surrendered—the rites were the same as receiving the edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the grand coordinator grand general's army returned and was about to enter the city, court ministers were dispatched to welcome them in the suburbs; the emperor attended the front hall; the grand coordinator led meritorious officials in offering thanks; the seal and edict were surrendered—the rites were the same as for receiving the edict.

sentences.zh: 宴禮既畢，兵部覈敘勛績，頒爵賞有差。

translations.literal: When the banquet rites were completed, the Ministry of War verified and recorded meritorious deeds and distributed ranks and rewards in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet rites were completed, the Ministry of War verified and recorded meritorious deeds and distributed ranks and rewards in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 厥後定邊將軍兆惠等、定西將軍阿桂等奏凱，高宗均駐蹕黃新莊行宮，築台郊勞，百官咸會。

translations.literal: Thereafter when Pacification-of-the-Frontier General Zhao Hui and others and Pacification-of-the-West General Agui and others reported victory, the Gaozong each time halted at the Huangxinzhuang traveling palace, built a platform for suburban welcome, and all officials assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter when Pacification-of-the-Frontier General Zhao Hui and others and Pacification-of-the-West General Agui and others reported victory, the Gaozong each time halted at the Huangxinzhuang traveling palace, built a platform for suburban welcome, and all officials assembled.

sentences.zh: 設黃幄正中，南鄉，兩翼青幕各八，東西鄉。

translations.literal: A yellow canopy was set in the center facing south; on each wing were eight green awnings facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: A yellow canopy was set in the center facing south; on each wing were eight green awnings facing east and west.

sentences.zh: 台在幄南，其上建左右纛，中設帝拜褥。

translations.literal: The platform was south of the canopy; on it left and right standards were erected and in the center the emperor's kneeling cushion was set.
translations.idiomatic: The platform was south of the canopy; on it left and right standards were erected, and in the center the emperor's kneeling cushion was set.

sentences.zh: 東西下馬紅柱各一。

translations.literal: On the east and west were one red dismounting post each.
translations.idiomatic: On the east and west was one red dismounting post each.

sentences.zh: 帝御龍袞詣台，鳴螺，奏鐃歌樂。

translations.literal: The emperor, in dragon robes, proceeded to the platform; conches sounded and naoge music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, in dragon robes, proceeded to the platform; conches sounded and naoge music was performed.

sentences.zh: 將軍暨從征大臣、將士皆擐甲胄，跪紅柱外俟駕。

translations.literal: The general and expedition ministers and soldiers all donned armor and knelt outside the red posts awaiting the imperial arrival.
translations.idiomatic: The general and the expedition ministers and soldiers all donned armor and knelt outside the red posts awaiting the imperial arrival.

sentences.zh: 帝就拜位立，將軍暨群臣班分東西，鴻臚官贊「跪」，則皆跪。

translations.literal: The emperor took his position at the kneeling place and stood; the general and officials were arranged in ranks east and west; when the Director of Ceremonies intoned "Kneel," all knelt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his position at the kneeling place and stood; the general and officials were arranged in ranks east and west; when the Director of Ceremonies intoned "Kneel," all knelt.

sentences.zh: 贊「叩，興」。

translations.literal: He intoned "Prostrate, rise."
translations.idiomatic: He intoned "Prostrate, rise."

sentences.zh: 帝拜天，三跪九叩，將軍等如之。

translations.literal: The emperor bowed to Heaven with three kneelings and nine prostrations, and the generals and others did likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed to Heaven with three kneelings and nine prostrations, and the generals and others did likewise.

sentences.zh: 畢，帝御幄升座，王公百官立東班幕下。

translations.literal: When finished, the emperor entered the canopy and ascended to his seat; imperial princes and officials stood beneath the eastern rank of awnings.
translations.idiomatic: When finished, the emperor entered the canopy and ascended to his seat; imperial princes and officials stood beneath the eastern rank of awnings.

sentences.zh: 禮成，帝出幄乘騎，凱歌作，奏鬯皇威章，駕還行宮。

translations.literal: When the rites were completed, the emperor left the canopy, mounted, the victory song was performed and the "Chang Huangwei" anthem played, and the imperial procession returned to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed, the emperor left the canopy and mounted; the victory song was performed and the "Chang Huangwei" anthem played, and the imperial procession returned to the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 餘依康熙間故事。

translations.literal: The rest followed the precedents of the Kangxi period.
translations.idiomatic: The rest followed the precedents of the Kangxi period.

sentences.zh: 咸豐五年，科爾沁親王僧格林沁平高唐亂。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianfeng, the Prince of Horqin Sengge Rinchen pacified the rebellion at Gaotang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Xianfeng, the Prince of Horqin Sengge Rinchen pacified the rebellion at Gaotang.

sentences.zh: 還朝日，文宗御養心殿，行抱見禮，慰勞備至。

translations.literal: On the day of his return to court, the Wenzong attended the Hall of Mental Cultivation and performed the embrace-audience rite, offering the fullest consolation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his return to court, the Wenzong attended the Hall of Mental Cultivation and performed the embrace-audience rite, offering the fullest consolation and reward.

sentences.zh: 先是出師頒參贊大臣關防，賜訥庫尼素光刀，至是同時獻納。

translations.literal: Earlier when setting out, the participating minister's seal had been issued and a Nekunisu gleaming blade bestowed; on this occasion both were presented and returned together.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when he set out, the participating minister's seal had been issued and a Nekunisu gleaming blade bestowed; on this occasion both were presented and returned together.

sentences.zh: 受降崇德二年春，朝鮮王服罪請降。

translations.literal: Receiving surrender: In the spring of the second year of Chongde, the King of Korea confessed guilt and sought to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving Surrender: In the spring of the second year of Chongde, the King of Korea confessed guilt and sought to surrender.

sentences.zh: 乃築壇漢江東岸，設黃幄，駕出營，樂作。

translations.literal: Then a platform was built on the east bank of the Han River, a yellow canopy was set up, the imperial carriage left camp, and music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: Then a platform was built on the east bank of the Han River, a yellow canopy was set up, the imperial carriage left camp, and music was performed.

sentences.zh: 濟江登壇，鹵簿具。

translations.literal: Crossing the river he ascended the platform, the imperial retinue complete.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the river he ascended the platform, the imperial retinue complete.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮王率陪臣步行來朝，遣官出迎一里外。

translations.literal: The King of Korea led his attending ministers on foot to come to court; officials were dispatched to welcome them one li out.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Korea led his attending ministers on foot to come to court; officials were dispatched to welcome them one li out.

sentences.zh: 引入，帝率同拜天，升座。

translations.literal: They were led in; the emperor led them in bowing to Heaven and ascended to his seat.
translations.idiomatic: They were led in; the emperor led them in bowing to Heaven and ascended to his seat.

sentences.zh: 國王等伏地請罪，贊「行三跪九拜禮」。

translations.literal: The king and others prostrated themselves to beg forgiveness; the intonation was "Perform the three kneelings and nine bows."
translations.idiomatic: The king and others prostrated themselves to beg forgiveness; the intonation was "Perform the three kneelings and nine bows."

sentences.zh: 賜坐，位列親王上，諸子列貝勒子。

translations.literal: Seats were granted; he was ranked above imperial princes, and his sons were ranked with beile's sons.
translations.idiomatic: Seats were granted; he was ranked above imperial princes, and his sons were ranked with beile's sons.

sentences.zh: 錫筵宴，還其俘，並賜王以下貂服。

translations.literal: A banquet was granted; their captives were returned; and sable robes were bestowed on the king and those below him.
translations.idiomatic: A banquet was granted; their captives were returned; and sable robes were bestowed on the king and those below him.

sentences.zh: 六年，蒙古貝勒等投誠，朝見已，命較射，選力士角牴，賜宴俾盡歡，殊典也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Mongol beile and others submitted in allegiance; after the audience they were ordered to compete in archery, strongmen were selected for wrestling, a banquet was granted to let them enjoy themselves fully—a special honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Mongol beile and others submitted in allegiance; after the audience they were ordered to compete in archery, strongmen were selected for wrestling, and a banquet was granted to let them enjoy themselves fully—a special honor.

sentences.zh: 所貢方物悉卻之。

translations.literal: All tribute items they presented were entirely declined.
translations.idiomatic: All tribute items they presented were entirely declined.

sentences.zh: 乾隆十四年，議制凡軍前受降，飛章入告。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong, regulations were deliberated: whenever surrender was received before the army, a rapid memorial was sent to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Qianlong, regulations were deliberated: whenever surrender was received before the army, a rapid memorial was sent to report.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 乃大書露布示中外，築壇大營左，南鄉。

translations.literal: Then a great announcement was written and displayed to court and country; a platform was built to the left of the main camp facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Then a great announcement was written and displayed to court and country; a platform was built to the left of the main camp facing south.

sentences.zh: 壇南百步外樹表，建大旗，書「奉詔納降」字。

translations.literal: A hundred paces south of the platform a marker post was erected and a great banner raised, bearing the words "Receiving Surrender by Imperial Decree."
translations.idiomatic: A hundred paces south of the platform a marker post was erected and a great banner raised, bearing the words "Receiving Surrender by Imperial Decree."

sentences.zh: 降者立其下，經略大將軍戎服出，鼓吹聲砲，參贊大臣等騎從。

translations.literal: The surrendering party stood beneath it; the grand coordinator grand general came out in military dress with drums, pipes, and cannon sounding; participating ministers and others followed on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendering party stood beneath it; the grand coordinator grand general came out in military dress with drums, pipes, and cannon sounding; participating ministers and others followed on horseback.

sentences.zh: 將至壇，降者北面匍伏，經略登壇正坐。

translations.literal: As he neared the platform, the surrendering party faced north and prostrated themselves; the grand coordinator ascended the platform and sat in the central place of honor.
translations.idiomatic: As he neared the platform, the surrendering party faced north and prostrated themselves; the grand coordinator ascended the platform and sat in the central place of honor.

sentences.zh: 參贊僉坐，諸將旁立，餘皆肅班行。

translations.literal: Participating ministers all sat together; various generals stood to the side; the rest all stood in orderly ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Participating ministers all sat together; various generals stood to the side; the rest all stood in orderly ranks.

sentences.zh: 降者膝行詣壇下，俯首乞命，經略宣上德意，量加賞賚。

translations.literal: The surrendering party crawled on their knees to the foot of the platform, bowed their heads and begged for their lives; the grand coordinator proclaimed the emperor's gracious intent and bestowed rewards according to measure.
translations.idiomatic: The surrendering party crawled on their knees to the foot of the platform, bowed their heads and begged for their lives; the grand coordinator proclaimed the emperor's gracious intent and bestowed rewards according to measure.

sentences.zh: 營門鼓吹殷然，降者泥首謝，興，退。

translations.literal: At the camp gate drums and pipes resounded loudly; the surrendering party bowed with foreheads to the ground in thanks, rose, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At the camp gate drums and pipes resounded loudly; the surrendering party bowed with foreheads to the ground in thanks, rose, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 獻俘受俘清初太祖、太宗以武功征服邊陲，俘虜甚眾，其時獻受猶無定制也。

translations.literal: Presenting captives and receiving captives: In the early Qing the Taizu and Taizong conquered the frontiers by military force and took very many captives; at that time there was as yet no fixed regulation for presenting and receiving them.
translations.idiomatic: Presenting Captives and Receiving Captives: In the early Qing the Taizu and Taizong conquered the frontiers by military force and took very many captives; at that time there was as yet no fixed regulation for presenting and receiving them.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年，討平青海，俘至京，始定諏吉先獻廟、社。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongzheng, after the pacification of Qinghai, when captives reached the capital, auspicious day selection was first fixed for presenting them at the temple and altars.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongzheng, after the pacification of Qinghai, when captives reached the capital, auspicious day selection was first established for presenting them at the temple and altars.

sentences.zh: 俘白組系頸，行及太廟街門外北鄉立，承祭官朝服至，俘伏，儀同時饗。

translations.literal: Captives, with white cords bound around their necks, were marched to stand facing north outside the gate of Taimiao Street; the officiating sacrificial official arrived in court dress; the captives prostrated themselves—the rites were the same as seasonal offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Captives, with white cords bound around their necks, were marched to stand facing north outside the gate of Taimiao Street; the officiating sacrificial official arrived in court dress; the captives prostrated themselves—the rites were the same as seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 至社稷街亦如之。

translations.literal: At Sheji Street it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: At Sheji Street it was likewise.

sentences.zh: 承祭官入壇致祭，儀同春、秋祈報。

translations.literal: The officiating sacrificial official entered the altar and performed the sacrifice—the rites were the same as the spring and autumn prayer and report ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The officiating sacrificial official entered the altar and performed the sacrifice—the rites were the same as the spring and autumn prayer and report ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 監俘者以俘出。

translations.literal: Those supervising the captives led the captives out.
translations.idiomatic: Those supervising the captives led the captives out.

sentences.zh: 翼日，帝御午門樓受俘，正中設御座，檐下張黃蓋，鹵簿陳闕門南北，仗馬次之。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor attended the Meridian Gate tower to receive captives; the imperial seat was set in the center; a yellow canopy was spread beneath the eaves; the imperial retinue was arrayed north and south of the palace gate, with guard horses next.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor attended the Meridian Gate tower to receive captives; the imperial seat was set in the center; a yellow canopy was spread beneath the eaves; the imperial retinue was arrayed north and south of the palace gate, with guard horses next.

sentences.zh: 輦輅陳金水橋南，馴象次之。

translations.literal: Imperial carriages were arrayed south of the Jinshui Bridge, with trained elephants next.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial carriages were arrayed south of the Jinshui Bridge, with trained elephants next.

sentences.zh: 王公百官咸集，解俘將校立金鼓外，俘後隨。

translations.literal: Imperial princes and officials all assembled; the officers escorting the captives stood outside the drums and gongs, with the captives following behind.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes and officials all assembled; the officers escorting the captives stood outside the drums and gongs, with the captives following behind.

sentences.zh: 班位既序，帝御龍袞，乘輿出宮，至太和門，大樂鐃吹，金鼓振作。

translations.literal: Once ranks were ordered, the emperor, in dragon robes, rode in the palanquin out of the palace to the Gate of Supreme Harmony; great music of bells and drums was performed and gongs and drums struck vigorously.
translations.idiomatic: Once ranks were ordered, the emperor, in dragon robes, rode in the palanquin out of the palace to the Gate of Supreme Harmony; great music of bells and drums was performed and gongs and drums struck vigorously.

sentences.zh: 登樓升座，贊「進俘」，丹陛大樂作，奏慶平章。

translations.literal: He ascended the tower and took his seat; the intonation was "Present the captives"; great music on the red steps was performed and the "Qing Ping" anthem played.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended the tower and took his seat; the intonation was "Present the captives"; great music on the red steps was performed and the "Qing Ping" anthem played.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚寺官引將校入，北面立，贊「行禮」，俘入匍伏。

translations.literal: An official of the Directorate of Ceremonies led the officers in; they stood facing north; the intonation was "Perform the rites"; the captives entered and prostrated themselves.
translations.idiomatic: An official of the Directorate of Ceremonies led the officers in; they stood facing north; the intonation was "Perform the rites"; the captives entered and prostrated themselves.

sentences.zh: 兵部官跪奏，平定某地所獲俘囚，謹獻闕下，請旨。

translations.literal: A Ministry of War official knelt and reported: the captives taken in pacifying such-and-such place are respectfully presented before Your Majesty—seeking instruction.
translations.idiomatic: A Ministry of War official knelt and reported: the captives taken in pacifying such-and-such a place are respectfully presented before Your Majesty—seeking instruction.

sentences.zh: 制曰：「所獻俘交刑部」。

translations.literal: The rescript read: "The captives presented are handed over to the Ministry of Punishments."
translations.idiomatic: The rescript read: "The captives presented are handed over to the Ministry of Punishments."

sentences.zh: 刑部長官跪領旨訖，械繫出。

translations.literal: The chief official of the Ministry of Punishments knelt to receive the rescript; when finished, the captives were bound with shackles and led out.
translations.idiomatic: The chief official of the Ministry of Punishments knelt to receive the rescript; when finished, the captives were bound with shackles and led out.

sentences.zh: 丹陛大樂作，王公百官行禮如常儀。

translations.literal: Great music on the red steps was performed; imperial princes and officials performed rites according to the usual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Great music on the red steps was performed; imperial princes and officials performed rites according to the usual protocol.

sentences.zh: 若恩赦不誅，則宣旨釋縛，俘叩首，將校引出。

translations.literal: If by gracious amnesty they were not executed, then the rescript was proclaimed to release their bonds; the captives knocked their heads in thanks and the officers led them out.
translations.idiomatic: If by gracious amnesty they were not executed, then the rescript was proclaimed to release their bonds; the captives kowtowed in thanks and the officers led them out.

sentences.zh: 是日賜將校宴兵部，次日賜冠履銀幣有差。

translations.literal: That day a banquet was granted to the officers at the Ministry of War; the next day caps, shoes, and silver coins were bestowed in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: That day a banquet was granted to the officers at the Ministry of War; the next day caps, shoes, and silver coins were bestowed in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 凡平定疆宇，受俘儀並同。

translations.literal: Whenever territory was pacified, the rites for receiving captives were all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever territory was pacified, the rites for receiving captives were all the same.

sentences.zh: 乾隆時，版圖日廓。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong period, the realm's borders expanded daily.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong period, the realm's borders expanded daily.

sentences.zh: 二十年，剿平準噶爾，獲達瓦齊暨青海羅卜藏丹津，先後檻入。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, the Dzungars were suppressed and pacified; Dawachi and Lubuzangdanjin of Qinghai were captured and successively sent in caged carts.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, the Dzungars were suppressed and pacified; Dawachi and Lubuzangdanjin of Qinghai were captured and successively sent to the capital in caged carts.

sentences.zh: 一歲中兩行斯典。

translations.literal: Within one year these ceremonies were performed twice.
translations.idiomatic: Within one year these ceremonies were performed twice.

sentences.zh: 越五年，底定回疆，討平攢拉促浸，皆遞舉盛儀。

translations.literal: Five years later, the Muslim regions were fully settled, and the Zunghar rebel faction was suppressed and pacified—all in succession occasioned grand ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later, the Muslim regions were fully settled and the Zunghar rebel faction was suppressed and pacified—all in succession occasioning grand ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 先後六歲，凱歌四奏，時論稱極盛雲。

translations.literal: Over six years in all, the victory song was performed four times; commentators of the time called it the height of glory.
translations.idiomatic: Over six years in all, the victory song was performed four times; commentators of the time called it the pinnacle of grandeur.

sentences.zh: 大閱天聰七年，太宗率貝勒等督厲眾軍，練習行陣，是為大閱之始。

translations.literal: Grand review: In the seventh year of Tiancong, the Taizong led beile and others to supervise and encourage the armies, practicing battle formations—this was the beginning of the grand review.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Review: In the seventh year of Tiancong, the Taizong led beile and others to supervise and encourage the armies, practicing battle formations—this was the beginning of the grand review.

sentences.zh: 順治十三年，定三歲一舉，著為令。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi it was fixed that it would be held once every three years and established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Shunzhi it was established that it would be held once every three years and made regulation.

sentences.zh: 尋幸南苑，命內大臣等擐甲胄，閱騎射，並演圍獵示群臣。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he visited the Southern Park, ordered inner ministers and others to don armor and helmets, reviewed mounted archery, and also staged encirclement hunts to display before the assembled officials.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he visited the Southern Park, ordered inner ministers and others to don armor, reviewed mounted archery, and also staged encirclement hunts for the assembled officials to observe.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年，閱兵南苑，聖祖擐甲，登晾鷹台，御黃幄，內大臣、都統等各束部曲，王、貝勒等各率旗屬，並自西而東。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kangxi, troops were reviewed at the Southern Park. The Shenzu donned armor, ascended the Falcon-drying Terrace, and took his seat beneath the yellow canopy. Inner ministers, commanders-in-chief, and others each marshaled their detachments; princes, beile, and others each led their banner subjects—and all proceeded from west to east.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Kangxi, troops were reviewed at the Southern Park. The Shenzu donned armor, ascended the Falcon-drying Terrace, and took his seat beneath the yellow canopy. Inner ministers, commanders-in-chief, and others each marshaled their detachments; princes, beile, and others each led their banner subjects, and all proceeded from west to east.

sentences.zh: 既成列，槍鳴號發，自東結陣馳以西，按翼分植。

translations.literal: Once ranks were formed, muskets sounded and signals fired; from the east they formed up and galloped westward, deploying by wing divisions.
translations.idiomatic: Once ranks were formed, muskets sounded and signals fired; from the east they formed up and galloped westward, deploying in wing divisions.

sentences.zh: 閱畢，命樹侯台上，親發五矢，皆中的，復騎而射，一發即中。

translations.literal: When the review was completed, he ordered a target set up on the platform; he personally loosed five arrows, all hitting the mark; then mounting again to shoot, he hit with a single shot.
translations.idiomatic: When the review was completed, he ordered a target set up on the platform and personally loosed five arrows, all hitting the mark; then, mounting again to shoot, he hit with a single shot.

sentences.zh: 釋甲賜宴，乃還。

translations.literal: They removed their armor, a banquet was granted, and he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: They removed their armor, a banquet was granted, and he then returned.

sentences.zh: 厥後行閱，或盧溝橋，或玉泉山，或多倫諾爾，地無一定，時亦不以三年限也。

translations.literal: Thereafter when traveling reviews were held, sometimes at Lugou Bridge, sometimes at Jade Spring Mountain, sometimes at Dolon Nor—the place was not fixed, and the timing was also not strictly bound to the three-year limit.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, traveling reviews were sometimes held at Lugou Bridge, sometimes at Jade Spring Mountain, sometimes at Dolon Nor—the location was not fixed, and the timing was not strictly bound to the three-year interval either.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，復幸南苑行閱，分八旗為三隊，帝率皇子擐甲，內大臣等扈從，後建龍纛三，上三旗侍衛隨行。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, he again visited the Southern Park for a traveling review. The Eight Banners were divided into three companies. The emperor led princes in donning armor, inner ministers and others attended in escort; behind them three dragon banners were erected, with guards from the Upper Three Banners accompanying the procession.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year, he again visited the Southern Park for a traveling review. The Eight Banners were divided into three companies. The emperor led princes in donning armor, with inner ministers and others in escort; behind them three dragon banners were erected, and guards from the Upper Three Banners accompanied the procession.

sentences.zh: 遍閱驍騎、護軍、前鋒、火器諸營。

translations.literal: He reviewed in turn the Vanguard Cavalry, Guard, Vanguard, and Firearms camps.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed in turn the Vanguard Cavalry, Guard, Vanguard, and Firearms camps.

sentences.zh: 立馬軍前，角螺鳴，伐鼓，行陣舁鹿角進。

translations.literal: Standing before the army on horseback, conch horns sounded, drums were beaten, and the battle lines advanced carrying deer-horn barriers.
translations.idiomatic: Standing before the army on horseback, he sounded conch horns and beat drums as the battle lines advanced carrying chevaux-de-frise.

sentences.zh: 甲士麾紅旗，槍砲齊發。

translations.literal: Armored soldiers waved red flags, and muskets and cannon fired together.
translations.idiomatic: Armored soldiers waved red flags, and muskets and cannon fired together.

sentences.zh: 鳴金止，再伐鼓，發槍砲如初。

translations.literal: Gongs sounded to halt; drums were beaten again, and muskets and cannon fired as before.
translations.idiomatic: Gongs sounded to halt; drums were beaten again, and muskets and cannon fired as before.

sentences.zh: 如是者九。

translations.literal: This was repeated nine times.
translations.idiomatic: This was repeated nine times.

sentences.zh: 初進率五丈，再進亦如之。

translations.literal: On the first advance they advanced five zhang; on the second advance it was likewise.
translations.idiomatic: On the first advance they moved forward five zhang; on the second advance they did the same.

sentences.zh: 至十進，槍砲環發無間。

translations.literal: By the tenth advance, muskets and cannon fired in a ring without pause.
translations.idiomatic: By the tenth advance, muskets and cannon were firing all around without pause.

sentences.zh: 開鹿角成八門，首隊出，二隊、三隊從。

translations.literal: The deer-horn barriers were opened to form eight gates; the first company went out, the second and third companies followed.
translations.idiomatic: The chevaux-de-frise were opened to form eight gates; the first company went out, and the second and third companies followed.

sentences.zh: 既成列，門闔，角鳴，呼譟進。
